reason: The cited evidence shows high-temperature DSC (E2) and DSC (E3) used for phase transformation temperatures and enthalpies, supporting the DSC premise. However, none of the cited passages describe integrating DSC with in situ dilatometry or X-ray imaging for volume measurement, leaving the core premise of simultaneous volume change determination entirely unsupported.
premises: High-temperature DSC can accurately measure melting temperature, enthalpy, and entropy of fusion in HEAs.
In situ dilatometry or X-ray imaging can be integrated with DSC to provide continuous volume change data.
The integrated method yields volume change at melting with sufficient accuracy.
The method is applicable across a broad compositional range of HEAs.
Calibration with reference materials ensures accuracy of temperature and enthalpy measurements.
